meta.title: Below the Record: A Philosophy of Nursing Science

center.label: My Philosophy of Nursing Science
text: Nursing science should study nursing as it's actually done, not as it's charted or scored.
That means treating the instrument as part of the question. Whether it's the chart, the NCLEX or a model, I ask what it counts, whose reasoning it treats as the standard, and what disappears.

Nursing work that doesn't enter the record doesn't exist to any system trained on that record. So nursing science has to make invisible work, and reasoning that works differently, knowable, without turning that knowledge into surveillance.

anchors.label: Nursing
anchors.subtitle: Scholarly operational definition
anchors.text: Nursing is the embodied, relational, reasoning work of noticing, interpreting and acting on a person's changing condition. It happens under real limits of staffing and acuity, and much of it never enters the record.

anchors.label: Science
anchors.subtitle: Scholarly operational definition
anchors.text: Science is systematic, accountable inquiry that makes its claims answerable to evidence. It also names what its instruments, categories and norms can't see.

clusters.label: Critical Realism
clusters.text: Reality exists whether or not we measure it, and our instruments only reach part of it. Care is real before it's charted. The record is a partial trace, not the thing itself.

clusters.label: Standpoint Theory & Black Feminist Thought
clusters.text: Knowledge comes from somewhere. Who's knowing shapes what gets known. My standpoint as a Black woman and a former bedside nurse is evidence I bring, not bias to scrub out.

clusters.label: Neurodiversity Paradigm
clusters.text: Neurocognitive variation is natural human diversity, not a deficit. Sound clinical judgment can take more than one cognitive shape, and our measures shouldn't treat one shape as the standard.

clusters.label: Critical Theory: Power & Surveillance
clusters.text: Knowledge is never separate from power. Data collected about nurses can be used to govern nurses. Nursing science has to ask who a measure serves.

clusters.label: Patterns of Knowing
clusters.text: Nursing knowledge is plural: empirical, ethical, personal, aesthetic and emancipatory. Empirical traces alone miss most of what a nurse knows.

clusters.label: Pragmatism
clusters.text: Theory and practice aren't separate. Knowledge proves itself in action. This shows up in my instinct to build measurable, usable fixes.

clusters.label: Logical Positivism
clusters.text: The view that only what's observable and measurable counts as knowledge. It's visible in my constellation as the position I push against, because it treats the record as the reality.

assumptions.label: Care is real before it's recorded
assumptions.text: Care is real before it's recorded, and beyond what gets recorded.

assumptions.label: No instrument is neutral
assumptions.text: Every measure builds in a norm, like the flowsheet or the CJMM.

assumptions.label: Judgment takes more than one shape
assumptions.text: Sound judgment can take more than one cognitive shape.

assumptions.label: Knowers have a standpoint
assumptions.text: Positionality is evidence, not bias to scrub out.

assumptions.label: Power travels with data
assumptions.text: Knowledge about nurses can be used against nurses.

assumptions.label: Nursing knowledge is plural
assumptions.text: Empirical, ethical, personal, aesthetic and emancipatory.
